source_text: Ταῦτα ὁ Εἰρήναιος ἀκολούθως ταῖς προδιεξοδευθείσαις ἡμῖν ὑπογραφὰς ἱστορίαις ἐν οἷς ἐπέγραφεν, πέντε οὐαὶ τὸν ἀριθμόν, Ἐλέγχου καὶ ἀνατροπῆς τῆς ψευδωνύμου γνώσεως, ἐν δευτέρῳ τῆς αὐτῆς ὑποθέσεως, ὅτι δὴ καὶ εἰς αὐτὸν ὑποδείγματα τῆς θείας καὶ παραδόξου δυνάμεως ἐν ἐκκλησίαις τισὶν ὑπολέλειπτο, διὰ τούτων ἐπισημαίνεται, λέγων· “τοσοῦτον δὲ ἀποδέουσιν τοῦ νεκρὸν ἐγεῖραι, καθὼς ὁ κύριος ἤγειρεν καὶ οἱ ἀπόστολοι διὰ προσευχῆς καὶ ἐν τῆ ἀδελφότητι πολλάκις διὰ τὸ ἀναγκαῖον καὶ τῆς κατὰ τόπον ἐκκλησίας πάσης αἰτησαμένης μετὰ νηστείας καὶ λιτανείας πολλῆς ἐπέστρεφεν τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ τετελευτηκότος καὶ ἐχαρίσθη ὁ ἄνθρωπος ταῖς εὐχαῖς τῶν ἁγίων.’’ καὶ αὗθίς φησιν μεθ’ ἕτερα· “εἰ δὲ καὶ τὸν κύριον φαντασιωδῶς τὰ τοιαῦτα πεποιηκέναι φήσουσιν, ἐπὶ τὰ προφητικὰ ἀνάγοντες αὐτούς, ἐξ αὐτῶν ἐπιδείξομεν πάντα οὕτως περὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ προειρῆσθαι καὶ γεγονέναι βεβαίως καὶ αὐτὸν μόνον εἶναι τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ· δι’ ὃ καὶ ἐν τῶ ἐκείνου ὀνόματι οἱ ἀληθῶς αὐτοῦ μαθηταί, πάρ’ αὐτοῦ λαβόντες τὴν χάριν ἐπιτελοῦσιν ἐπ’ εὐεργεσίᾳ τῆ τῶν λοιπῶν ἀνθρώπων, καθὼς εἷς ἕκαστος τὴν δωρεὰν εἴληφεν παρ’ αὐτοῦ. οἱ μὲν γὰρ δαίμονας ἐλαύνουσιν βεβαίως καὶ ἀληθῶς, ὥστε πολλάκις καὶ πιστεύειν ἐκείνους αὐτοὺς τοὺς καθαρισθέντας ἀπὸ τῶν πονηρῶν πνευμάτων καὶ εἶναι ἐν τῆ ἐκκλησίᾳ, οἱ δὲ καὶ πρόγνωσιν ἔχουσιν τῶν μελλόντων καὶ ὀπτασίας καὶ ῥήσεις προφητικάς, ἄλλοι δὲ τοὺς κάμνοντας διὰ τῆς τῶν χειρῶν ἐπιθέσεως ἰῶνται καὶ ὑγιεῖς ἀποκαθιστᾶσιν, ἤδη δέ, καθὼς ἔφαμεν, καὶ νεκροὶ ἠγέρθησαν καὶ παρ’. σὺν ἡμῖν ἔτεσιν ἱκανοῖς, καί, τί γάρ; οὐκ δ’ ἔστιν ἀριθμὸν εἰπεῖν τῶν χαρισμάτων ὧν κατὰ παντὸς τοῦ κόσμου ἢ ἐκκλησία παρὰ θεοῦ λαβοῦσα ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ χριστοῦ τοῦ σταυρωθέντος ἐπί Ποντίου Πιλάτου ἑκάστης ἡμέρας ἐπ’ εὐεργεσίᾳ τῇ τῶν ἐθνῶν ἐπιτελεῖ, μήτε ἐξαπατῶσά τινας μήτε ἐξαργυριζομένη· ὡς γὰρ δωρεὰν εἴληφεν παρὰ θεοῦ, δωρεὰν καὶ διακονεῖ.’’ καὶ ἐν ἑτέρῳ δὲ τόπῳ ὁ αὐτὸς γράφει· “καθὼς καὶ πολλῶν ἀκούομεν ἀδελφῶν ἐν τῆ ἐκκλησίᾳ προφητικὰ χαρίσματα ἐχόντων καὶ παντοδαπαῖς λαλούντων διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος καὶ τὰ κρύφια τῶν ἀνθρώπων εἰς φανερὸν ἀγόντων ἐπὶ τῷ συμφέροντι καὶ τὰ μυστήρια τοῦ θεοῦ ἐκδιηγουμένων ” ταῦτα καὶ περὶ τοῦ διαφορὰς χαρισμάτων μέχρι καὶ τῶν δηλουμένων χρόνων παρὰ τοῖς ἀξίοις διαμεῖναι.
pass_a_gloss: These things Irenaeus follows the previously narrated histories, in which he wrote, five books, of the Exposure and Overthrow of the falsely-named knowledge, in the second of the same hypothesis, that indeed also to him examples of the divine and paradoxical power in some churches were left, through these things it is pointed out, saying: 'so much they are able to raise the dead, just as the Lord raised and the apostles through prayer and in the brotherhood often through the necessary and the whole church in the place having asked with much fasting and supplication the spirit of the deceased returned and the man was given to the prayers of the saints.' And again he says after other things: 'if indeed they will say that the Lord fantastically did such things, leading them to the prophetic things, from these things we will show all things thus about him and were spoken beforehand and happened certainly and he alone is the Son of God; through which also in his name the true disciples of him, having received the grace from him, perform for the benefit of the other men, just as each one received the gift from him. For some drive out demons certainly and truly, so that often even those who were cleansed from the evil spirits believe and are in the church, some have foreknowledge of the things to come and visions and prophetic sayings, others heal the sick through the laying on of hands and restore them to health, and already, as we said, even the dead were raised and with us for many years, and what? is it not the case that there is no number to the gifts which the church receives from God in the name of Jesus Christ, the crucified one, under Pontius Pilate, every day for the benefit of the nations, neither deceiving anyone nor being bribed; for just as it was received as a gift from God, it is also served as a gift.' And in another place the same man writes: 'just as we hear of many brothers in the church having prophetic gifts and speaking in various ways through the Spirit and bringing the hidden things of men to light for their benefit and narrating the mysteries of God' these things also about the differences of gifts remain even until the times indicated by the worthy ones.

choices.english: in the second of the same hypothesis

pass_b_english: Irenaeus follows the historical accounts that have been previously narrated, and in his five books, Exposure and Overthrow of the Falsely-Named Knowledge, he provides examples of the divine and paradoxical power that was evident in some churches, as he points out in the second part of his work. He notes that the Lord and the apostles were able to raise the dead through prayer and the support of their community, and that this same power was still present in the churches, where the Holy Spirit would return to the deceased in response to the fervent prayers and fasting of the entire church. Irenaeus also argues that if some people claim the Lord's miracles were just fantasies, he can use Scripture to demonstrate the truth about Him and show that He is the Son of God. The true disciples of the Lord, having received His grace, use their gifts to benefit others, just as they received them from Him. Some drive out demons, and those who have been freed from evil spirits often become believers and join the church. Others have foreknowledge of future events, receive visions, or speak prophetically, while some heal the sick through the laying on of hands, restoring them to health. In fact, even the dead have been raised back to life, and this has been happening for many years, demonstrating the countless gifts that the church receives from God in the name of Jesus Christ, who was crucified under Pontius Pilate. These gifts are used every day for the benefit of all nations, without deceiving or bribing anyone, because they are given freely by God and served freely by the church. Irenaeus also writes about the various gifts that many brothers in the church have received, including prophetic gifts that allow them to speak in different ways, guided by the Spirit, and to reveal hidden things for the benefit of others, as well as to share the mysteries of God. These gifts, with all their differences, will remain until the time indicated by those who are worthy.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text, including the specific terminology regarding Irenaeus's work and the description of the charismatic gifts. Pass A provides a literal translation and Pass B provides a fluent rendering that preserves all arguments, agency, and theological distinctions. The note correctly identifies that no direct scripture citations are present in the Greek text despite the mention of 'prophetic things'.
